methods: rearranging to a quadratic in x
statement: Find the range of the function $f(x)=\dfrac{x^{2}+1}{x^{2}+x+1}$ for real $x$.
solution: Set $y=\dfrac{x^{2}+1}{x^{2}+x+1}$. Rearranging gives $(y-1)x^{2}+yx+(y-1)=0$. For real $x$ the discriminant must be non-negative: $\Delta=y^{2}-4(y-1)^{2}=-3y^{2}+8y-4\ge 0$, i.e. $3y^{2}-8y+4\le 0=(3y-2)(y-2)\le 0$. Hence $\tfrac23\le y\le 2$, which is the range.
hints: Write $y=f(x)$ and rearrange into a quadratic in $x$.
Require the discriminant to be non-negative.
